title: Canary mesh + cost-safety telemetry for batching & caching experiments
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Scope: Build a lightweight canary mesh and cost-safety telemetry layer to safely A/B test batching and KV-caching configuration changes (batch size targets, dynamic batching window, prefix-KV TTLs, prefetch policies). This ticket covers experiment design, automated rollout & rollback rules, metric collection contracts, and dashboards for ops & product analysis. Goal: enable automated experiments that reduce unit token cost while preserving tail latency SLOs and model quality.

Background: Previous batch/cache experiments reduced token cost but occasionally regressed p95/p99 latency or had subtle quality impacts for small cohorts. We need a standardized experimentation scaffold that:
- isolates cohorts by traffic slice (customer tier, API key type)
- monitors dual safety signals (latency SLO + quality/semantic regression)
- behaves as a canary mesh allowing many concurrent micro-experiments with independent telemetry and automated safe rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Can run concurrent experiments for different batching and KV-configs (at least 3 simultaneous)
Automated rollout with exposure ramp: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with configurable waits
Automated rollback triggers on multi-metric rules (latency SLO breach OR quality regression > 1.5% OR cost increase)
Grafana dashboards for cost/latency/quality by cohort and experiment id
Analysis notebook template + SQL queries to compute statistically valid lift and CI
Playbook documented in Confluence with runbook steps and incident links
success_criteria: Demonstrable experiment that reduces per-1k-token cost by >=7% for at least one workload cohort without increasing p99 latency by >5ms and without model quality regressions beyond the agreed threshold.
experiment_plan:
Design: use Bayesian sequential A/B framework with dual endpoints (cost-per-1k-token, and p99 latency) and monitoring of a proxy quality metric (LLH delta on a fixed eval prompt set + sampled human-label checks). Cohorts: random user-key based assignment stratified by customer tier and region. Minimum sample size per ramp stage computed by running traffic-replay estimates (expected mean and variance from last 7 days). Statistical decision rules encoded in 'experiment-service' to avoid stopping early due to noise.

Exposure schedule: 0.5% (24h) -> 5% (48h) -> 20% (72h) -> 100% (1 week) with health checks at each stage. Each stage requires: min samples reached AND no safety triggers fired for the preceding wait window.

Safety thresholds (initial):
- p99 latency relative increase > 7% OR absolute increase > 15ms -> fail
- SLO error-rate (>= 95th token error) increase > 0.5% -> fail
- Proxy quality (LLH) posterior probability of regression > 0.95 for >1.5% delta -> fail
- Cost increase > 2% -> treat as neutral/fail depending on product goal
rollout_plan: Implement integration with 'orch-controller' to push config changes to runtime. Orchestrate traffic-split via gateway tagging keys. Rollout controller exposes API to advance/rollback a stage. By default, the rollout is manual-approve at the 5% and 20% transitions; emergency auto-rollback will occur if any safety trigger fires. Provide a CLI command: 'rwd exp advance --id=ENG-58102' and 'rwd exp rollback --id=ENG-58102'.
dashboards: Grafana: EXP-Canary-Mesh overview (experiment_id, cohort, exposure, decision_state)
Grafana: EXP-Cost-Latency Scatter (cost vs p99 by cohort)
Grafana: EXP-Batch-Cache Telemetry (batch-size distribution, kv-hit heatmap)
Redwood Console: Per-route token economics (linked to experiment ids)
Looker: Experiment summary table (lift, CI, decision)
analysis_plan: After each stage, run the analysis notebook (Python + Arviz for Bayesian posteriors). Compute posterior distributions for cost delta and latency delta. Use hierarchical modeling to borrow strength across similar cohorts and detect heterogenous effects. Produce a short findings doc: executive summary, per-cohort lifts/regressions, suggested next config. For quality signals, automatically surface any eval prompt regressions > 1%. Keep an audit trail of sampled prompts and human labels (stored in secure S3).
rollback_rules: Immediate auto-rollback if p99 latency increases by >7% or >15ms absolute at stage window
Auto-rollback if proxy quality posterior indicates >95% probability of >1.5% regression
Manual rollback recommendation if cost increases but latency and quality are unchanged (requires PM approval)
Rollback record logged in experiment-service with cause, metric snapshot, and related PR/commit
updates: 2025-02-19: Initial scoping with PM and Observability. Agreed to use Bayesian sequential instead of fixed-hypothesis tests to reduce false positives for small cohorts. (Aisha)
2025-02-22: Infra spike complete: experiment-service prototype can register experiments and store cohort assignments. Generated sample telemetry from traffic-replay. (Tomás)
2025-02-26: Dashboard templates created in Grafana (EXP-Canary-Mesh overview + cost-latency scatter). Waiting on final labels for customer-tier stratification. (Nora)
2025-03-01: Safety thresholds reviewed with SRE and Research. Adjusted p99 relative threshold from 5% -> 7% after benchmarking noisy tails. (SRE review: see PR 1432)
2025-03-04: Draft runbook uploaded to Confluence; PR #1897 adds CLI hooks to advance/rollback experiments. Requesting design review for UX of console exposure controls. (Tomás)
notes: This ticket intentionally separates telemetry + decision logic from optimizer recommendations. The next phase will integrate autotuner suggestions into experiment-service once the safety scaffold is stable. Consider targeted dark launches for high-value enterprise customers before broad rollout.
